_comment: Migration scenario suite. Weight: 3 = most production integrations need it, 2 = common, 1 = occasional. Channels are imported from Mirth 4.5 exports; their scripts are written in GalvaniFlow's scripting API, as an operator rewrites them when moving (D-244: no E4X or Mirth script APIs). Frozen once approved; changing it resets the baseline.

scenarios.title: MLLP listener returns the ACK its postprocessor builds
Lane router sends each message type to one lane through queued Channel Writers
Transformer edits HL7 fields and deletes a segment
Channel calls code templates imported with the server backup
JSON report is sent as an ORU to the configuration-map host
Queued TCP sender delivers after an outage and errors on a NACK
HTTP listener routes on context path and returns the postprocessor JSON
JavaScript Writer reports SENT with a reply, or ERROR by throwing
Messages reach a channel picked at run time and an audit channel by name
Messages are found by their ACCESSION metadata column
JavaScript Reader polls on an interval and keeps a counter in $gc
SMTP Sender sends a mail with a subject from the channel map
ADT filtered, mapped to JSON, sent to HTTP and Postgres, retried, reprocessed
Database Reader turns new Postgres rows into HL7 and marks them sent
Database Writer inserts rows into MySQL
File Reader over SFTP reads a partner file and deletes it
HTTP Sender sends Basic auth, query parameters and substituted values
TCP listener accepts STX/ETX framing and answers in the same framing
Delimited CSV rows are read by column name
X12 270 member id is read with msg.get
HL7 batch file is split into one message per MSH
Destination error triggers an alert email naming the channel

scenarios.source: anti-gaming B4: 3 disabled channels in the prod backup
scenarios.title: A channel disabled in Mirth is imported disabled
Code template libraries apply only to the channels Mirth enabled them for
A listener that responds before processing answers AA even when its transformer fails
